prompt: Explain waste segregation and why separating at source matters.
hook: Sorting at the bin beats sorting at the dump.

card.oneLiner: Separating waste into wet, dry and hazardous streams at source makes composting and recycling possible and keeps landfills smaller.
keyPoints: Wet waste can be composted or digested.
Dry waste can be recycled if it is clean and separated.
Hazardous and sanitary waste need separate handling.
Mixed waste becomes unrecoverable and goes to landfill.

framework.name: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016
framework.gloss: Duty to segregate waste into specified streams.

whatYouCanDo: Keep separate bins for wet, dry and hazardous waste.
Rinse and dry recyclables before handing them over.
Ask your local body how collected waste is processed.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Local collection systems vary widely.

sources.title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

prompt: Explain the rules on single-use plastic and how plastic is phased out.
hook: Some plastic is banned; the rest still needs managing.

card.oneLiner: India bans a list of single-use plastic items and sets extended producer responsibility for packaging, while thinner carry bags are also restricted.
keyPoints: Certain single-use items are prohibited.
Packaging carries producer responsibilities for collection and recycling.
Minimum thickness rules apply to carry bags.
Enforcement and alternatives remain practical challenges.

framework.name: Plastic Waste Management Rules
framework.gloss: Rules on plastic waste, thickness and single-use items.

framework.name: Central Pollution Control Board
framework.gloss: Monitoring and guidance on plastic waste management.

whatYouCanDo: Carry reusable bags, bottles and cutlery.
Refuse single-use items when you can.
Return packaging where take-back systems exist.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. The banned list and rules change over time.

sources.title: Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change

prompt: Explain landfills, leachate and why legacy waste is a problem.

card.oneLiner: Landfills generate methane and a toxic liquid called leachate, and old accumulation or 'legacy' waste dumps are now being cleared and remediated.
keyPoints: Decomposing organic waste releases methane.
Leachate can seep into soil and groundwater.
Old dumps are being biomined to recover land.
Reducing waste at source shrinks the problem.

framework.name: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016
framework.gloss: Standards for sanitary landfills and legacy waste.

whatYouCanDo: Compost wet waste so less reaches the landfill.
Ask whether your city has a sanitary landfill.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Remediation is slow and site-specific.

sources.title: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

prompt: Explain Extended Producer Responsibility for packaging.
hook: The maker cleans up, not just the buyer.

card.oneLiner: Extended Producer Responsibility makes producers responsible for collecting and recycling the packaging they put on the market, backed by targets.
keyPoints: Producers must meet collection and recycling targets.
Obligations can be met through certificates.
It shifts the cost of waste from taxpayers to producers.
Monitoring and data quality are the hard part.

framework.name: Extended Producer Responsibility guidelines
framework.gloss: Targets and certificate mechanisms for producers.

framework.name: Central Pollution Control Board
framework.gloss: Registration and reporting for obligated entities.

whatYouCanDo: Support brands that take back packaging.
Check whether your city's recyclers are formalised.
Understand that EPR needs enforcement to work.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Rules and targets are revised over time.

prompt: Explain composting and how households and cities turn waste into a resource.

card.oneLiner: Composting turns wet waste into a soil amendment, cutting methane from landfills and returning nutrients to the soil.
keyPoints: Microbes break down organic waste into compost.
Home bins suit households; cities compost at scale.
Composting avoids the methane made in landfills.
The finished compost improves soil and saves water.

framework.name: Solid Waste Management Rules, 2016
framework.gloss: Preference for processing wet waste locally.

framework.name: Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs

whatYouCanDo: Start a home or society compost bin.
Avoid putting cooked and oily food in dry recyclables.
Use finished compost in gardens and common areas.
card.caveats: Educational information, not professional advice. Composting needs the right mix of greens, browns and air.
